wa_andersons_thumb_standard.name: Honeymoon Meadows
wa_andersons_thumb_standard.note: Forested backcountry camp with reliable creek water; the West Fork ford here can run high and hazardous in spring or after heavy rain, and mosquitoes are thick in summer.

wa_andersons_thumb_standard.name: Anderson Pass
wa_andersons_thumb_standard.note: Trail junction where the West Fork Dosewallips and East Fork Quinault routes cross; the Anderson Pass Shelter (Camp Siberia) sits just below at roughly 4,180 ft.

wa_andersons_thumb_standard.name: Anderson Tarn high camp
wa_andersons_thumb_standard.note: Small tarn camp reached via a steep mile of wildflower slopes above the pass; last reliable camp before committing to the glacier.

wa_andersons_thumb_standard.name: Flypaper Pass
wa_andersons_thumb_standard.note: Gain point onto the Eel Glacier via a snow finger, named for the dark rocks scattered across the ice below; the finger typically melts out by late summer, so climb it early season.

wa_andersons_thumb_standard.name: Eel Glacier bergschrund / headwall
wa_andersons_thumb_standard.note: Downward traverse around a rock buttress onto the upper Eel Glacier; the bergschrund opens wide late-season and glacier recession has steepened this slope to 40+ degrees in spots.

wa_andersons_thumb_standard.name: West Fork Dosewallips Trailhead (Dose Forks)
wa_andersons_thumb_standard.note: Current DB value (47.7413,-123.0474) is misplaced near the Dosewallips Road washout gate off Hwy 101, ~8-9 trail miles short of the real trailhead.

wa_boston_peak_southeast_face.name: Boston Basin Trailhead
wa_boston_peak_southeast_face.note: Small pullout on Cascade River Road, mile ~21.7, opposite Johannesburg Mountain. Mountaineers.org lists this route as 'Boston Peak/Southeast Face via Quien Sabe Glacier' — the SE Face is reached by climbing up from Boston Basin high camp toward the Sahale/Quien Sabe Glacier area and traversing to the face, not via a separate road trailhead. Existing DB value (48.475,-121.075) was close but imprecise; corrected to the sourced pullout location.

wa_boston_peak_west_face.name: Eldorado Creek trailhead (Cascade River Road mile 20)

wa_soviet_route.name: Hart Lake
wa_soviet_route.note: Reliable, ice-cold water source and the last easy camp option before the route's steep terraces begin, per Cascade Alpine Guide beta.

wa_soviet_route.name: Rock and heather terraces
wa_soviet_route.note: Steep, loose rock-and-heather terraces gain most of the ~3,000 ft to high camp; exposed Class 3-4 scrambling in spots.

wa_soviet_route.name: High camp near North Star-Bonanza pass (~7,100 ft)
wa_soviet_route.note: Flat, parklike camp with water available, about 2.5 hours above Hart Lake, just south of the pass between North Star Mountain and Bonanza's Southwest Peak.

wa_soviet_route.name: Buttress base
wa_soviet_route.note: Under an hour across talus from camp to the start of the route, roughly 60 ft above the buttress's lowest point; first pitch is a narrow chimney.

wa_soviet_route.name: Crux pitches, middle third of buttress
wa_soviet_route.note: Three sustained pitches of 5.9-5.10a in the middle of the route, the technical crux above a horizontal bypass ledge and cave belay.

wa_soviet_route.name: Northeast Ridge traverse to West Peak
wa_soviet_route.note: Exposed, gendarmed ridge traverse (~2 hr) from the Southwest Peak to the West Peak before dropping off the NW side via talus and two ~200-ft rappels.

wa_soviet_route.name: Holden Village / Railroad Creek Trailhead
wa_soviet_route.note: Via ferry+bus to Holden Village, then Railroad Creek Trail ~3.5mi to Hart Lake (3,956ft), then off-trail up rock/heather terraces ~3,000ft to a camp near the 7,100ft pass between Bonanza and North Star Peak, then talus to the buttress base.

wa_buckhorn_marmot_pass.name: Upper Big Quilcene Trailhead (Trail #833.1)
wa_buckhorn_marmot_pass.note: Reached via FR 27 (Big Quilcene River Road) then FR 2750, ~4.75 mi to trailhead; the existing DB trailhead coordinate is wrong, it sits near Marmot Pass rather than the actual road trailhead

wa_burgundy_spire_north_face.name: SR-20 Pullout (Burgundy Col climbers' trail)
wa_burgundy_spire_north_face.note: Same pullout as the other two routes; directly corroborated by this route's own recorded GPS track (trackStart 48.55143,-120.63097). The existing DB trailhead ('Early Winters Creek Trailhead', 48.532,-120.61) appears to be a data error — it is ~1.5 mi from this location and unsupported by any source or by the route's own track.

wa_chianti_spire_east_face.name: Chianti Spire / East Face (Rebel Yell) area
SR-20 Pullout near Milepost 166 (Burgundy Col approach)
wa_chianti_spire_east_face.note: Unmarked highway pullout ~2-4 miles east of the Washington Pass hairpin turn; climbers descend to Early Winters Creek then switchback up to Burgundy Col. Coordinate taken from this route's recorded GPS track start, which matches sourced approach descriptions geographically. Existing DB value ('Early Winters Creek Trailhead') is a likely mismatch with a different, unrelated hiking trailhead.

wa_chimney_rock_east_face_direct.name: East Face Direct - base of climb

wa_dark_peak_dark_glacier_route.name: High Bridge / Agnes Creek Trailhead (Stehekin Valley Road)
wa_dark_peak_dark_glacier_route.note: Reached only via Lady of the Lake ferry from Chelan to Stehekin (no road access), then NPS shuttle bus up-valley to High Bridge; hike Agnes Creek Trail ~5mi to Five Mile/Swamp Creek Camp, then follow the abandoned, overgrown Swamp Creek Trail/drainage up to the Dark Glacier.

wa_narcos.name: Cutthroat Creek Wall / Little Liberty Bell
wa_narcos.note: No established trail; hike through woods then traverse rocky benches to the wall base, ~1-1.5 hrs. Narcos is a 5.9 trad, PG13 line.

wa_narcos.name: Cutthroat Creek Trailhead
wa_narcos.note: Turn off Hwy 20 ~4.4-4.5mi east of Washington Pass onto FR-400 (signed for Cutthroat Lake/Creek Trail), drive ~1mi to trailhead lot (restrooms). From the trailhead, leave trail and bushwhack/hike up through open forest (no maintained trail) toward the wall, gaining elevation and traversing left; ~1-1.5hr to the base. This matches the existing DB entry exactly.

wa_narcos.name: Little Liberty Bell / Cutthroat Creek Wall (formation high point)

wa_wright_pond.name: Cutthroat Creek Wall / Little Liberty Bell
wa_wright_pond.note: No established trail; hike through woods then traverse rocky benches to the wall base, ~1-1.5 hrs. Wright-Pond is a 5.11a/b trad, PG13 line.

wa_wright_pond.name: Cutthroat Creek Trailhead
wa_wright_pond.note: Same trailhead/approach as Narcos — both routes are on the same small wall, reached via the Cutthroat Creek Trail/FR-400 trailhead off Hwy 20.

wa_wright_pond.name: Little Liberty Bell / Cutthroat Creek Wall (formation high point)

wa_ahoot.name: Middle Point Trailhead (FR 64)
wa_ahoot.note: Drive ~1.5 miles further south on FR 64 past this trailhead, then a short scramble up to Minidike's base.

wa_czech_it_out.name: Megadike South
wa_czech_it_out.note: South end of the same megadike wall as Megadike North; park ~1.2 mi past the trailhead just before the river bridge, scramble up the NW hillside above the bridge abutment, then traverse the ridge to the south-facing walls.

wa_czech_it_out.name: Middle Point Trailhead (FR 64)
wa_czech_it_out.note: Drive ~1.2 miles further south on FR 64 past this trailhead, then scramble up the hillside to Megadike.

wa_firearms.name: Minidike
wa_firearms.note: Smaller of the two closely-spaced fins at the core of The Dikes; park ~1.5 mi past the trailhead just after the river bridge, cross the road, scramble down the abutment, and follow the trail downstream on the NW bank.

wa_firearms.name: Middle Point Trailhead (FR 64)
wa_firearms.note: Drive ~1.5 miles further south on FR 64 past this trailhead, then a short scramble up to Minidike's base.

wa_heinous_thing.name: Megadike South
wa_heinous_thing.note: South end of the same megadike wall as Megadike North; park ~1.2 mi past the trailhead just before the river bridge, scramble up the NW hillside above the bridge abutment, then traverse the ridge to the south-facing walls.

wa_heinous_thing.name: Middle Point Trailhead (FR 64)
wa_heinous_thing.note: Drive ~1.2 miles further south on FR 64 past this trailhead, then scramble up the hillside to Megadike.

wa_internal_combustion.name: Minidike
wa_internal_combustion.note: Smaller of the two closely-spaced fins at the core of The Dikes; park ~1.5 mi past the trailhead just after the river bridge, cross the road, scramble down the abutment, and follow the trail downstream on the NW bank.

wa_internal_combustion.name: Middle Point Trailhead (FR 64)
wa_internal_combustion.note: Drive ~1.5 miles further south on FR 64 past this trailhead, then a short scramble up to Minidike's base.

wa_just_for_fun.name: Minidike
wa_just_for_fun.note: Smaller of the two closely-spaced fins at the core of The Dikes; park ~1.5 mi past the trailhead just after the river bridge, cross the road, scramble down the abutment, and follow the trail downstream on the NW bank.

wa_just_for_fun.name: Middle Point Trailhead (FR 64)
wa_just_for_fun.note: Drive ~1.5 miles further south on FR 64 past this trailhead, then a short scramble up to Minidike's base.

wa_moe.name: Megadike South
wa_moe.note: South end of the same megadike wall as Megadike North; park ~1.2 mi past the trailhead just before the river bridge, scramble up the NW hillside above the bridge abutment, then traverse the ridge to the south-facing walls.

wa_moe.name: Middle Point Trailhead (FR 64)
wa_moe.note: Drive ~1.2 miles further south on FR 64 past this trailhead, then scramble up the hillside to Megadike.

wa_redtail_arete.name: Megadike South
wa_redtail_arete.note: South end of the same megadike wall as Megadike North; park ~1.2 mi past the trailhead just before the river bridge, scramble up the NW hillside above the bridge abutment, then traverse the ridge to the south-facing walls.

wa_redtail_arete.name: Middle Point Trailhead (FR 64)
wa_redtail_arete.note: Drive ~1.2 miles further south on FR 64 past this trailhead, then scramble up the hillside to Megadike.

wa_safety_dance.name: Megadike South
wa_safety_dance.note: South end of the same megadike wall as Megadike North; park ~1.2 mi past the trailhead just before the river bridge, scramble up the NW hillside above the bridge abutment, then traverse the ridge to the south-facing walls.

wa_safety_dance.name: Middle Point Trailhead (FR 64)
wa_safety_dance.note: Drive ~1.2 miles further south on FR 64 past this trailhead, then scramble up the hillside to Megadike.

wa_dorado_needle_east_ridge.name: Col between Pt. 8386 and Dorado Needle (East Ridge start)
Eldorado Trailhead (Cascade River Road)
wa_dorado_needle_east_ridge.note: Existing DB value (48.492611,-121.117611) appears incorrect — does not match the confirmed roadside trailhead used by the other three Dorado Needle routes; recommend correcting to this value

wa_east_mcmillan_spire_west_ridge.name: Cairn / Terror Basin Route split
wa_east_mcmillan_spire_west_ridge.note: Cairn marks where the climbers' path leaves the old logging roadbed and angles south of Terror Creek, climbing steeply toward treeline.

wa_east_mcmillan_spire_west_ridge.name: Terror Basin Camp
wa_east_mcmillan_spire_west_ridge.note: Gravelly, wildflower-covered basin with established tent sites and running snowmelt streams — the standard high camp shared by parties climbing any of the McMillan Spires.

wa_east_mcmillan_spire_west_ridge.name: Basin notch above camp
wa_east_mcmillan_spire_west_ridge.note: Notch just above camp gives a view down to Lake Azure and the glaciated cliffs below; from here the route crosses basin slabs and snow benches toward the East-West McMillan col.

wa_east_mcmillan_spire_west_ridge.name: Snow gully below East-West McMillan col
wa_east_mcmillan_spire_west_ridge.note: Steep snow/scree gully estimated in the 40-degree range on the approach to the col — crampons and axe essential; this is also the descent line, so watch for rockfall and parties below.

wa_east_mcmillan_spire_west_ridge.name: East-West McMillan Col
wa_east_mcmillan_spire_west_ridge.note: Crux decision point where the steep snow gully and the 4th-class rock ledge variant both top out before the final scramble to the East summit block.

wa_east_mcmillan_spire_west_ridge.name: Goodell Creek Trail Trailhead (climbers' access near Upper Group Campground)
wa_east_mcmillan_spire_west_ridge.note: Corrects existing DB point, which is ~1.1km south and appears to mark the campground entrance rather than the actual trail start; new coordinate corroborated by both Trailforks and our recorded GPS track's start point.

wa_east_twin_needle_south_route.name: Terror Creek logjam crossing
wa_east_twin_needle_south_route.note: Climbers' path fades to bushwhack here; cross Terror Creek on a large logjam (last reliable water before the steep, cliffy push up toward the Barrier).

wa_east_twin_needle_south_route.name: The Barrier ridge crossing
wa_east_twin_needle_south_route.note: Loose, exposed scrambling (harder late-season without snow cover) gains this ridge that separates the Terror Creek drainage from Crescent Creek Basin.

wa_east_twin_needle_south_route.name: Crescent Creek Basin (Chopping Block Camp)
wa_east_twin_needle_south_route.note: Established bivy sites on the saddle below Mount Terror, used as base camp for both Twin Needles; talus/scree basin below the south-facing summit gullies.

wa_east_twin_needle_south_route.name: Eye Col
wa_east_twin_needle_south_route.note: Class-5 chockstone squeeze gains the notch between the summit gullies shared with West Twin Needle; rope up for this section.

wa_east_twin_needle_south_route.name: Goodell Creek Trailhead (Cross-Country Zone Access, Upper Goodell Creek)
wa_east_twin_needle_south_route.note: Confirmed by AAC Publications ('Lower Goodell Creek trailhead' used for East Twin Needle North Buttress), Wikipedia ('Goodell Creek Cross-Country Zone Access Trailhead', RT 19.5 mi, 600-7936ft), and a detailed trip report (onehikeaweek.com) describing the same Goodell Creek Trail -> Terror Creek ford -> The Barrier -> Crescent Creek Basin -> Eye Col approach used for all Twin Needles routes. Existing DB coordinate matches the documented trailhead location near the Upper Goodell Creek Group Camp/gravel-pit parking area and was not changed.

wa_east_twin_needle_south_route.name: East Twin Needle
wa_east_twin_needle_south_route.note: Wikipedia (citing Twin Needles as a pair) gives one shared coordinate for the complex, 48.77667N/121.31250W, and states the peaks lie ~0.55 mi west of Mount Terror (48.7743N/121.2996W, per Wikipedia's Mount Terror article) - the existing DB point at 48.768,-121.288 is southeast of Terror, the wrong direction, and appears incorrect. A trip report (onehikeaweek.com) independently confirms East Twin Needle sits atop 'Eye Col' immediately adjacent to West Twin Needle. No source gives East and West Twin Needle fully separate coordinates, so this point is nudged slightly east of the shared Wikipedia coordinate toward Eye Col/Mount Terror to approximate the 'East' summit specifically; treat it as an approximation good to a few hundred meters, not an exact surveyed point.

wa_glacier_view_temple.name: Keechelus Ridge parking area (off FR 4934)
wa_glacier_view_temple.note: I-90 Exit 54, north on FR 4832 ~4 mi, left on FR 4934, pass Mount Margaret Trailhead, continue ~3 mi to small parking area on right; ~25-30 min uphill hike/scramble to the East Face wall. Shared by all East Face routes including Project Crack.

wa_glacier_view_temple.name: East Face wall top-out, Keechelus Ridge
wa_glacier_view_temple.note: Not a mountain summit — single-pitch crag; climbers top out directly above the route at the cliff edge, essentially the same location as the crag itself.

wa_project_crack.name: Keechelus Ridge parking area (off FR 4934)
wa_project_crack.note: Same shared approach as all East Face routes: I-90 Exit 54, FR 4832, FR 4934, ~25-30 min hike to the wall.

wa_project_crack.name: East Face wall top-out, Keechelus Ridge
wa_project_crack.note: Not a mountain summit — single-pitch crag; top-out is directly above the route line.

wa_plan_9_from_outer_space.name: Goodell Creek Trailhead (Terror Basin / Crescent Creek Basin approach)
wa_plan_9_from_outer_space.note: Standard access point for all Southern Pickets objectives via Hwy 20 near Newhalem; not route-specific beta, but no other approach is documented for this remote buttress.

wa_plan_9_from_outer_space.name: Ed Wood Memorial Buttress / Plan 9 from Outer Space start

wa_junior_s_farm.name: The Full Montey (Junior's Farm topout)
wa_junior_s_farm.note: 8-pitch sport/alpine route (5.9) at Tyler Peak Crags in Olympic National Forest; topout elevation is approximate.

wa_junior_s_farm.name: The Full Montey / Junior's Farm base area
Tyler Peak Trailhead
wa_junior_s_farm.note: Unmarked trailhead off FR 2870/2860 (turn at spur sign '270'), ascends a boulder field to the Mossness Wall; same approach used for The Full Montey / Junior's Farm.

wa_blood_sport.name: Blood Sport crag
wa_blood_sport.note: Short (~50') isolated crag low on the mountain, just around the corner from the main West Face, near the base of South Rib.

wa_blood_sport.name: Alpental Ski Area / Snow Lake Trailhead parking lot
wa_blood_sport.note: Existing DB trailhead (47.4453,-121.4234) is essentially correct — matches published Snow Lake TH coordinates. Blood Sport is reached by heading up the boot path/old Sahale ski track from this lot and traversing east along the base of Guye Peak's south rib (Mountain Project: 'passed when traversing east along the base of the South Rib route').

wa_ephemeral.name: Ice Box right side topout
wa_ephemeral.note: Corrected coordinate - matches this area's own registered location (Ice Box right side, Hairpin Crags, Washington Pass) and the real Ice Box left side crag used by nearby routes (Iceman, Route C, Route D) in this same database.

wa_ephemeral.name: Ice Box right side / Ephemeral base
Hairpin Turn pullout (Hwy 20 roadside parking, Washington Pass)
wa_ephemeral.note: Roadside pullout at the highway's hairpin switchback just east of Washington Pass; no permit required. This is the Mountain Project-listed coordinate for Hairpin Crags itself ('park at the hairpin' is the entire approach instruction) — there is no separately surveyed parking pin distinct from the crag location.

wa_ephemeral.name: Ice Box (right side) formation, Hairpin Crags
wa_ephemeral.note: Not a distinct mountain summit — a slab/gully rock formation that routes top out on. Elevation is an estimate carried over from the adjacent, similarly-elevationed Ice Box left side listing (5,490 ft) since Mountain Project does not give a separate elevation for the right side.

wa_j_tnar.name: Jötunheim Wall Topout (Middle Peak)
wa_j_tnar.note: 16-pitch, Grade VI big wall (5.9 A3+) with bolted anchors and portaledge bivies; best climbed late July-early Sept before snowmelt turns pitches into waterfalls.

wa_j_tnar.name: Lake Serene Trailhead (Mount Index Rd / Trail 1068)
wa_j_tnar.note: Existing DB value confirmed exact match to sourced coordinates. Hike the Lake Serene trail then traverse talus/scree around the lake's south/west side into the Norwegian Buttress cirque; this is the only approach used for all routes in this cirque (Jötnar, Mjolnir, Bluebell, etc.).

wa_northeast_ridge_1963_route.name: Cascade Pass
wa_northeast_ridge_1963_route.note: Maintained trail tops out here; leave it for the climbers' path toward Johannesburg.

wa_northeast_ridge_1963_route.name: Cascade River Crossing / Terminal Moraine
wa_northeast_ridge_1963_route.note: Off-trail descent and ford of the infant Cascade River below the terminal moraine.

wa_northeast_ridge_1963_route.name: Base of C-J Couloir
wa_northeast_ridge_1963_route.note: Gain rock just before the Cascade-Johannesburg couloir narrows; the NE Ridge (1963) climbs the rib right of the couloir.

wa_northeast_ridge_1963_route.name: Hanging Glacier Traverse
wa_northeast_ridge_1963_route.note: Exposed rising traverse beneath Johannesburg's hanging glaciers; rockfall and icefall hazard.

wa_northeast_ridge_1963_route.name: Cascade Pass Trailhead (end of Cascade River Road)
wa_northeast_ridge_1963_route.note: Corrects existing DB pin, which sits ~1.2km southeast of the actual NPS trailhead parking loop; two independent sources (WTA, 10adventures) agree closely on this coordinate.

wa_klawatti_peak_sw_buttress.name: Klawatti camp / col
wa_klawatti_peak_sw_buttress.note: Camp south of Klawatti near the col dividing the Klawatti and McAllister Glaciers; SW Buttress start is minutes away.

wa_klawatti_peak_sw_buttress.name: Eldorado Trailhead (Cascade River Road, Mile 20)
wa_klawatti_peak_sw_buttress.note: Existing DB trailhead (48.4926,-121.1176) is likely wrong — should be corrected to this shared Eldorado Creek Trailhead, same as the SE Face route.

wa_liberty_cap_ptarmigan_ridge_finish.name: Columbia Crest (historic high point; overtaken by the crater's southwest rim per an Aug. 2024 GPS survey as the icecap thins)

wa_spontaneous_distraction.name: Le Petit Cheval Upper Mountain
wa_spontaneous_distraction.note: Shared upper section for Le Petit Cheval's multi-pitch routes.

wa_spontaneous_distraction.name: Milepost 165 Pullout, SR-20
wa_spontaneous_distraction.note: Climbers' trail starts at the far west end of the Milepost 165 pullout, crosses Early Winters Creek, then traverses an avalanche path (three fixed-rope sections) toward the base of the formation; ~1.5hr approach. A faster alternative uses the gully paralleling Spontaneity Arete.

wa_tooth_and_claw.name: Lexington Tower East Shoulder (topout)
wa_tooth_and_claw.note: Confirmed via Mountain Project - this route climbs Lexington Tower's East Face, Washington Pass. Coordinate is medium confidence (formation-level, from an AI-summarized page fetch rather than a directly visible lat/lon field).

wa_tooth_and_claw.name: Lexington Tower / Tooth and Claw (Mountain Project marker)
Pond pullout near hairpin turn (SR 20), E of Washington Pass — shared start with East Face

wa_little_mac_spire_southwest_route.name: Goodell Creek Crossings
wa_little_mac_spire_southwest_route.note: Trail fords two branches of Goodell Creek that run high on hot afternoons; a small streamside campsite sits near the second crossing.

wa_little_mac_spire_southwest_route.name: Terror Creek Cairn / Climbers' Path
wa_little_mac_spire_southwest_route.note: Large cairn and stone arrow mark the turn off the maintained Goodell Creek trail onto the steep, faint climbers' path south of Terror Creek — matches the on-file '~4,000 ft over 2 mi' push.

wa_little_mac_spire_southwest_route.name: Rocky Streambed Source
wa_little_mac_spire_southwest_route.note: Last dependable water on the climbers' path, running in a rocky streambed; the faint tread resumes just upstream.

wa_little_mac_spire_southwest_route.name: Terror Basin Notch
wa_little_mac_spire_southwest_route.note: Gap on the east rim of Terror Basin reached via a rising traverse over moderate snow into midsummer; first view down onto the basin and the McMillan/Little Mac group.

wa_little_mac_spire_southwest_route.name: Terror Basin Camp
wa_little_mac_spire_southwest_route.note: Shared high camp for the whole McMillan/Terror cluster — flat gravel benches, running water, and rock-walled bivy sites; base for Little Mac, East Mac, and West Mac.

wa_little_mac_spire_southwest_route.name: Loose Rock Below the Summit Block
wa_little_mac_spire_southwest_route.note: Southern Pickets rock is notoriously fractured here; test holds and stagger climbers on the short 5.4 pitch to avoid knocking rock onto partners below.

wa_little_mac_spire_southwest_route.name: Goodell Creek Trailhead
wa_little_mac_spire_southwest_route.note: Standard, single approach for all Southern Pickets/Terror Basin objectives including Little Mac Spire. Existing DB point (48.6733,-121.2658, 'Goodell Creek Group Campground Trailhead') is ~1.1km south of the actual trail start and appears to be the campground rather than the trailhead itself; corrected coordinate matches the sourced Goodell Creek trailhead location almost exactly.

wa_little_mac_spire_southwest_route.name: Little Mac Spire
wa_little_mac_spire_southwest_route.note: Approximate — no independently surveyed summit coordinate found for this minor Southern Pickets spire; cross-referenced against neighboring McMillan/Terror group summits and the route's recorded approach track to place it as close to the true high point as available sources allow.

wa_traverse_of_mount_index.name: Lake Serene (approach basin below North Peak)
Lake Serene Trailhead (Bridal Veil Falls TH, US-2 near Index, WA)
wa_traverse_of_mount_index.note: Traverse starts 'at the lake' (Lake Serene basin) and climbs the skyline right-to-left, summiting North Peak first then continuing over Middle and Main.

wa_traverse_of_mount_index.name: Mount Index - North Peak (first of three summits climbed on the traverse)

wa_blood_orgy.name: Top of Mamie Peak wall
wa_blood_orgy.note: Blood Orgy is reached by rappel off Woodland Critter Christmas, or via a short 5.10 pitch starting up it; Mamie Peak's true summit (6,108') is easy scrambling above.

wa_blood_orgy.name: Hannegan Pass Trailhead
wa_blood_orgy.note: Existing DB value confirmed correct; USFS/WTA list trailhead near 48.9105,-121.5894 to 48.9102,-121.592 (road-end parking, slight variance by source but same location).

wa_ellation.name: Top of Ellation
wa_ellation.note: 8-pitch, ~700' 5.11a (or 5.10 A0) up shallow grooves above the crag.

wa_hail_satan.name: Top of Mamie Peak wall
wa_hail_satan.note: Multi-pitch line on the same crag as Ellation and Blood Orgy.

wa_mcclellan_peak_southwest_scramble.name: Snow Lakes Trailhead
wa_mcclellan_peak_southwest_scramble.note: 4.2 mi south on Icicle Creek Rd (FR-76) from junction with US-2, Leavenworth. Existing DB coord (47.5556, -120.705) is ~1.3 mi off but in the same immediate area/road; corrected to the FS-listed parking lot coordinate.

wa_woodland_critter_christmas.name: Top of Mamie Peak wall
wa_woodland_critter_christmas.note: Access pitch that connects into Blood Orgy via rappel or continued 5.10 climbing.

wa_woodland_critter_christmas.name: Mamie Peak crag (near base of Ellation)

wa_honeymoon_route.name: Royal Lake
wa_honeymoon_route.note: Via Upper Dungeness Trail from Royal Basin trailhead; exact trailhead coordinates could not be confidently verified so only Royal Lake and the summit are included.

wa_honeymoon_route.name: Upper Dungeness Trailhead
wa_honeymoon_route.note: Standard approach for the only documented route on Mount Deception: hike the Royal Basin Trail (#833.2) ~7.2 miles to Royal Lake, then the Upper Royal Basin Trail into the alpine basin, then scramble to the summit ridge. Accessed via Forest Roads 2880/2870 from Sequim/Palo Alto Rd.

wa_moss_out_for_harambe.name: Barlow Pass trailhead (Mountain Loop Highway)
wa_moss_out_for_harambe.note: Same trailhead as Gothic Basin/Monte Cristo townsite trail; gated end of pavement, ~31 mi east of Granite Falls. Existing DB value (48.0265,-121.444) matches closely.

wa_poltergeist_pinnacle.name: Hannegan Pass
wa_poltergeist_pinnacle.note: Trail crests here; continue cross-country toward the Chilliwack drainage and Whatcom Pass.

wa_poltergeist_pinnacle.name: Boundary Camp
wa_poltergeist_pinnacle.note: Camp in the Chilliwack River valley below the climb to Whatcom Pass.

wa_poltergeist_pinnacle.name: Whatcom Pass
wa_poltergeist_pinnacle.note: Gap between Whatcom Peak and the Challenger massif; gateway to Challenger Glacier.

wa_poltergeist_pinnacle.name: Challenger Glacier Crossing
wa_poltergeist_pinnacle.note: Roped glacier travel across Challenger Glacier; crevasse hazard.

wa_poltergeist_pinnacle.name: Hannegan Pass Trailhead (Trail #674)
wa_poltergeist_pinnacle.note: Matches existing DB entry (48.91021, -121.591885) to within ~150m — same trailhead, minor coordinate rounding difference. This is the sole approach used for all Northern Pickets objectives near Mount Challenger; route continues via Whatcom Pass and Perfect Pass (~6300 ft) before a multi-mile crossing of the Challenger Glacier to reach the pinnacle.

wa_you_moss_be_joking.name: Barlow Pass trailhead (Mountain Loop Highway)
wa_you_moss_be_joking.note: Same trailhead as Moss Out For Harambe — both routes are on the same formation. Existing DB value (48.0265,-121.444) matches closely.

wa_mount_lyall_south_route.name: Holden Village / Holden Lake Trailhead
wa_mount_lyall_south_route.note: Shuttle drop-off at the former mining village; the Holden Lake Trail begins on the west side of town along Holden Road, following the Railroad Creek valley.

wa_mount_lyall_south_route.name: Holden Lake Trail turnoff (Hart/Lyman Lake Trail junction)
wa_mount_lyall_south_route.note: After about a mile paralleling Railroad Creek, bear right off the Hart/Lyman Lake trail onto the Holden Lake Trail and begin climbing switchbacks.

wa_mount_lyall_south_route.name: Avalanche chute crossings
wa_mount_lyall_south_route.note: Trail crosses several open, south-facing avalanche chutes on dry terrain; tread can be faint and brushy through slide alder after big snow years.

wa_mount_lyall_south_route.name: Holden Lake
wa_mount_lyall_south_route.note: Glacial basin lake with established camping and reliable water; Bonanza Mountain's Mary Green Glacier is visible across the valley — good base camp for the summit push.

wa_mount_lyall_south_route.name: Basin below Holden Pass
wa_mount_lyall_south_route.note: Leave the trail here and head off-trail cross-country up open basins toward Holden Pass, the jumping-off point for the south-facing talus/heather slopes to Lyall's summit.

wa_mount_lyall_south_route.name: Lucerne Landing (Lake Chelan) via Holden Village shuttle
wa_mount_lyall_south_route.note: No road access; reached only by Lady of the Lake passenger ferry from Chelan (~40 mi uplake) to the Lucerne dock, then the Holden Village shuttle (FS Rd 8301, ~11 mi) to Holden, from where trails up Railroad/Tenmile/Company Creek lead to the Tenmile Pass/Hilgard Pass basins used to climb Lyall. Existing DB coordinate (48.20188,-120.59921) was already essentially correct — refined here to the more precisely sourced Lucerne coordinate (48°12'08"N 120°35'28"W).

wa_mount_norton_scramble.name: Mary's Falls Camp
wa_mount_norton_scramble.note: Established backcountry campsite beside the Elwha River with reliable water; roughly the halfway point to Elkhorn and a common overnight stop for the long approach.

wa_mount_norton_scramble.name: Elkhorn Guard Station
wa_mount_norton_scramble.note: Historic 1911 backcountry patrol cabin and grassy river-flat camp; last reliably maintained camp before leaving the main Elwha corridor toward Norton.

wa_mount_norton_scramble.name: Hayes River Guard Station
wa_mount_norton_scramble.note: Elwha River Trail meets the Hayes River here (16.1 mi from Whiskey Bend per NPS); climbers leave the maintained trail near this junction and head up the Hayes River drainage toward Norton's east slopes.

wa_mount_norton_scramble.name: Off-trail ascent below Norton's east face
wa_mount_norton_scramble.note: No path or cairns beyond Hayes River — dense slide alder and devil's club in the lower brush belt give way to open Class 2 heather/talus higher up; the east aspect gains about 3,200 ft in under a mile, so route-find carefully in fog or low visibility.

wa_mount_norton_scramble.name: Whiskey Bend Trailhead
wa_mount_norton_scramble.note: Start of the Elwha River Trail; existing DB coordinate (47.9643,-123.5844) is within ~0.3mi of this and effectively the same trailhead. From Whiskey Bend the route follows the Elwha River Trail roughly 16+ miles south to the Hayes River area before leaving trail for the class 2 scramble to Norton's summit.

wa_mount_olson_standard.name: South Fork Skokomish River ford
wa_mount_olson_standard.note: Unbridged ford of the Skokomish's south bank; safely crossable (ankle-deep) only in late summer/early fall low water per WTA, otherwise a serious hazard.

wa_mount_olson_standard.name: Olympic National Park boundary
wa_mount_olson_standard.note: Trail leaves Olympic National Forest and enters Olympic National Park/Wilderness; self-issue backcountry camping permit required beyond this point, tread grows fainter above here.

wa_mount_olson_standard.name: Sundown Pass
wa_mount_olson_standard.note: Forested saddle marked by a broken signpost, reached via steep, faint tread through wet subalpine meadows; junction with the Six Ridge Trail heading east along the crest toward Mount Olson.

wa_mount_olson_standard.name: Lake Sundown
wa_mount_olson_standard.note: Short spur off the pass to a subalpine basin lake on Six Ridge's western flank; last dependable water and the standard base camp for an Olson attempt.

wa_mount_olson_standard.name: Six Ridge crest / Mount Olson boot-path junction
wa_mount_olson_standard.note: Point on Six Ridge's sawtooth crest closest to Olson where an unsigned, unofficial boot path ('Mount Olson Way') leaves the trail for the peak; faint and overgrown with blowdowns and lingering snowfields into midsummer.

wa_mount_olson_standard.name: Tarn below Olson's summit block
wa_mount_olson_standard.note: Boulder-field tarn just below the summit block is the last water and a common bivy spot; the final gully above it to the top is steep, loose, and exposed per trip reports.

wa_mount_olson_standard.name: Upper South Fork Skokomish Trailhead (Trail #873)
wa_mount_olson_standard.note: Existing DB coordinate (47.4794,-123.4521) is close (~1km off) but the USFS-published trailhead coordinate is more precise. Reached via Skokomish Valley Rd / FS-23 / FS-2361 from Shelton; FS-2361 gated Oct 1-Apr 30. Standard route follows Trail 873 to Sundown Lake, then the Six Ridge crest ~11 miles to the overgrown 'Mount Olson Way' spur.

wa_ridge_traverse_from_east_fury.name: Access Creek Junction
wa_ridge_traverse_from_east_fury.note: Leave Big Beaver Trail to ascend Access Creek toward the Southern Pickets.

wa_ridge_traverse_from_east_fury.name: Access Col
wa_ridge_traverse_from_east_fury.note: Gains the crest between Access Creek and Luna Cirque.

wa_ridge_traverse_from_east_fury.name: Luna Col
wa_ridge_traverse_from_east_fury.note: High col below Luna Peak; standard approach to the Fury massif.

wa_ridge_traverse_from_east_fury.name: Loose Tower Traverse
wa_ridge_traverse_from_east_fury.note: Descend to a low saddle then climb over three loose towers, low 5th class; rope recommended for rappels.

wa_ridge_traverse_from_east_fury.name: Ross Dam Trailhead (SR-20) — via Ross Lake water taxi/hike to Big Beaver, then off-trail to Access Creek/Luna Camp
wa_ridge_traverse_from_east_fury.note: Road-accessible trailhead on SR-20 (MP 134-135) at Ross Dam/Ross Lake Resort. Parties either walk ~6 mi along the west shore of Ross Lake or take the Ross Lake Resort water taxi to the Big Beaver Trail junction, hike ~9.4 mi up Big Beaver Trail to Luna Camp, then go off-trail up Access Creek to the Luna-Fury col before climbing East Fury and traversing the connecting ridge (three towers) to reach West Fury. This is the standard approach corridor for essentially all Picket Range 'northern group' peaks including both East and West Fury; existing DB trailhead (48.71,-121.058) is close to but not exactly on this corridor — it sits between the Ross Dam trailhead and the Big Beaver Creek/Ross Lake confluence (~48.776,-121.058).

wa_mount_shuksan_hanging_glacier.name: White Salmon Road (hairpin) TH
wa_mount_shuksan_hanging_glacier.note: Corrects existing DB value of Lake Ann TH. Hairpin turn onto NF-3075 off SR542 near mile 51-52, just before the White Salmon Day Lodge.

wa_sherpa_glacier.name: Sherpa Glacier toe/icefall
wa_sherpa_glacier.note: Glacier terminates as an icefall here; crevasses present, cross high where the glacier is flatter.

wa_sherpa_glacier.name: Top of Sherpa Glacier
wa_sherpa_glacier.note: Tops out at the notch gaining Mount Stuart's upper North Ridge.

wa_sherpa_glacier.name: Stuart Lake Trailhead (end of FR 7601, Eightmile Creek Rd)

wa_upper_north_ridge_w_great_gendarme.name: Top of Sherpa Glacier notch
wa_upper_north_ridge_w_great_gendarme.note: Ascend Sherpa Glacier to this notch to gain the upper North Ridge, bypassing the lower ridge's early pitches.

wa_upper_north_ridge_w_great_gendarme.name: Esmeralda Basin / Ingalls Lake Trailhead (North Fork Teanaway Rd, FR 9737)
wa_upper_north_ridge_w_great_gendarme.note: DB currently lists Stuart Lake TH (Eightmile Creek Rd) — appears to be an error; this specific 'Upper' route variant is guided/documented via the Ingalls Lake side to skip the lower ridge

wa_clast_from_the_past.name: Pinto Rock topout (approximate)
wa_clast_from_the_past.note: Approximate - research confirms a short (~0.3mi) documented climbers trail from the pullout to the formation, but no exact topout coordinate was found; this reuses the pullout coordinate with a disclosed ~0.3mi uncertainty rather than a precise fix.

wa_clast_from_the_past.name: North Side wall (Mountain Project GPS pin)
Pinto Rock Pullout (North Side)
wa_clast_from_the_past.note: Roadside pullout on NF-77 (via NF-25 -> NF-28 -> NF-77 from Randle, WA) directly below Pinto Rock; matches existing DB entry exactly.

wa_flycatcher_buttress.name: Base of Flycatcher Buttress
wa_flycatcher_buttress.note: Stay right of the gully dividing the two spires, scrambling to a flat ledge at the start.

wa_flycatcher_buttress.name: Hairpin Turn pullout (SR-20)
wa_flycatcher_buttress.note: East-side approach — NOT Blue Lake TH. MP route text explicitly names the Hairpin as the start point.

wa_sidewinder_4.name: Pinto Rock topout (approximate)
wa_sidewinder_4.note: Approximate - research confirms a short (~0.3mi) documented climbers trail from the pullout to the formation, but no exact topout coordinate was found; this reuses the pullout coordinate with a disclosed ~0.3mi uncertainty rather than a precise fix.

wa_sidewinder_4.name: North Side wall (Mountain Project GPS pin)
Pinto Rock Pullout (North Side)
wa_sidewinder_4.note: Same pullout as the other North Side routes; MP route page notes the approach trail is 'extremely steep and loose.'

wa_top_gun.name: Pinto Rock topout (approximate)
wa_top_gun.note: Approximate - research confirms a short (~0.3mi) documented climbers trail from the pullout to the formation, but no exact topout coordinate was found; this reuses the pullout coordinate with a disclosed ~0.3mi uncertainty rather than a precise fix.

wa_top_gun.name: North Side wall (Mountain Project GPS pin)
Pinto Rock Pullout (North Side)
wa_top_gun.note: Same pullout/approach as Sidewinder and Clast from the Past; MP describes Top Gun as a toprope reached by lowering from Sidewinder's anchor chains to the roof lip, i.e. same base approach, not a separate trailhead.

wa_lone_wolf.name: FR-9070 / PCT (#2000) junction near Olallie Meadow, Snoqualmie Pass
wa_lone_wolf.note: This is the well-documented point where FR-9070 crosses the PCT (per WTA's Silver Peak trailhead directions: I-90 exit 54, Hyak Drive NE becomes FR-9070, 5.4 mi to the PCT crossing). Mountain Project's Citidel approach says climbers then take the LEFT fork of FR-9070 past this junction and drive/walk to 'a large turnaround just below Silver Basin' (20-30 min approach on foot from there to the crag base) — that further turnaround has no separately published name or coordinate, so this junction is the closest sourced reference point, not the exact parking spot. Confidence is medium because of that gap.

wa_lone_wolf.name: The Obelisk (rock formation/crag), Silver Basin
wa_lone_wolf.note: Elevation is an estimate from the surrounding terrain (Citidel base area is listed at 4,585 ft; The Obelisk sits further up-slope from the Sofa King Buttress sub-area, per MP's own text) — MP does not publish a separate elevation figure for this formation.

wa_ottohorn_southeast_route.name: Large cairn off the old roadbed
wa_ottohorn_southeast_route.note: Cairn/arrow marks where the climbers' path leaves the Goodell Creek roadbed toward Terror Creek and Crescent Creek Basin, per multiple trip reports of this same junction.

wa_ottohorn_southeast_route.name: Terror Creek ford
wa_ottohorn_southeast_route.note: Ford on foot near a cairn on the far bank; typically no more than calf-deep by midsummer but can run high and cold earlier in the season.

wa_ottohorn_southeast_route.name: Forested ridge crest, toe of the Barrier
wa_ottohorn_southeast_route.note: Steep climbers' path tops out on the ridge between Terror and Crescent Creeks here; this is the base of 'the Barrier' rock rib you cross next.

wa_ottohorn_southeast_route.name: The Barrier crossing
wa_ottohorn_southeast_route.note: Loose, dirty Class 3 traverse with exposed moves crossing the Barrier's rock rib into the Terror/Crescent Creek basins; rockfall risk on the loose sections.

wa_ottohorn_southeast_route.name: Crescent Creek Basin camp
wa_ottohorn_southeast_route.note: Established basin camp used for Ottohorn, Himmelhorn, and the Chopping Block; reached after crossing the Barrier.

wa_ottohorn_southeast_route.name: Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col
wa_ottohorn_southeast_route.note: About an hour above camp with some dicey scrambling near the top; gain the col here then follow the 1961 line onto Ottohorn's east ridge (Class III). South side of the col is the easier descent, the north side turns to loose low-5th once melted out.

wa_ottohorn_southeast_route.name: Goodell Creek Trailhead
wa_ottohorn_southeast_route.note: Unpaved pullout off Goodell Creek Rd, just before Goodell Creek Campground, across SR-20 from Newhalem; standard access for all Southern Pickets objectives via the Terror Creek climbers' trail.

wa_pernod_spire_standard.name: Burgundy Col
wa_pernod_spire_standard.note: "7,770-ft notch separating the Wine Spires from Vasiliki Ridge, reached via steep talus/scree above the Bench camp."

wa_pernod_spire_standard.name: SR-20 Wine Spires pullout / Burgundy Col climbers' trail
wa_pernod_spire_standard.note: Corrects existing DB value; see wa_direct_west_face note for the same trailhead description.

wa_point_success_south_side.name: Indian Henry's Hunting Ground (patrol cabin)
wa_point_success_south_side.note: Historic 1915 patrol cabin marks where the route leaves the maintained Wonderland Trail for cross-country travel toward the Mirror Lakes basin.

wa_point_success_south_side.name: Mirror Lakes
wa_point_success_south_side.note: Small tarns about a mile off the Wonderland Trail; last dependable water before contouring dry southwest/west slopes of Pyramid Peak.

wa_point_success_south_side.name: Point 6631 (base camp north of Pyramid Peak)
wa_point_success_south_side.note: Flat campsites just north of this 6,631 ft high point give broad views of Success Cleaver; no sourced GPS fix found, position estimated from route beta contouring Pyramid Peak.

wa_point_success_south_side.name: 6,400 ft saddle below Success Cleaver
wa_point_success_south_side.note: Short descent NNE from Point 6631 to this saddle; typical high camp before scrambling onto the lower cleaver at first light.

wa_point_success_south_side.name: Lower Success Cleaver gendarmes
wa_point_success_south_side.note: Loose rock towers force weaving route-finding on the lower rib; rockfall risk climbs if other parties are above, per trip reports citing bivy options around 8,100-8,300 ft.

wa_point_success_south_side.name: Rockfall chutes to Kautz Cleaver headwall
wa_point_success_south_side.note: Angle across three loose, rockfall-swept chutes to the headwall and gain the Kautz Cleaver near 12,600 ft; helmet mandatory, best crossed before sun loosens rock.

wa_point_success_south_side.name: Westside Road / Dry Creek (Tahoma Creek) Trailhead
wa_point_success_south_side.note: End of driveable Westside Road (3.2 mi from the Nisqually-Longmire Rd junction), gated at Dry Creek. Existing DB value (Longmire Wilderness Information Center) is a permit/ranger station ~3.5 miles away, not the actual trailhead. This point sits ~30m from the recorded track's start (46.795212, -121.88138), strongly corroborating it.

wa_remmel_mountain_nw_ridge.name: Four Point Lake
wa_remmel_mountain_nw_ridge.note: Multiple good campsites with views of Remmel; standard bivy.

wa_remmel_mountain_nw_ridge.name: NW Ridge Camp
wa_remmel_mountain_nw_ridge.note: Bivy on Remmel's NW Ridge itself, reached via ridge travel from the Four Point Lake basin.

wa_remmel_mountain_nw_ridge.name: Thirtymile Trailhead
wa_remmel_mountain_nw_ridge.note: Existing DB coordinate (48.835, -120.068) is ~4km off from the true trailhead; corrected per WTA.org and Natural Atlas. From here, follow Chewuch River Trail #510 to Remmel Lake, then go off-trail south (~2 miles bushwhack) to reach the NW Ridge, per a documented 2011 ascent trip report.

wa_ruth_icy_traverse.name: Hannegan Pass
wa_ruth_icy_traverse.note: Leave the maintained trail; climbers path heads east/south around a shoulder toward Ruth Glacier.

wa_ruth_icy_traverse.name: Ruth Glacier Camp
wa_ruth_icy_traverse.note: Common high camp on Ruth Mountain's north slope.

wa_ruth_icy_traverse.name: Ruth-Icy Saddle
wa_ruth_icy_traverse.note: Descend a west-facing snow slope from Ruth to this connecting saddle.

wa_ruth_icy_traverse.name: Hannegan Trailhead (Hannegan Pass Trail #674 road end)
wa_ruth_icy_traverse.note: Road end of Forest Road 32 (Ruth Creek/Hannegan Pass Rd) at Hannegan Campground, ~12.5 mi east of Glacier, WA on Mt Baker Hwy SR 542 then 5.3 mi up FR 32. Hike Hannegan Pass Trail 4 mi to Hannegan Pass (5,056 ft), then climbers' trail east/south onto the north side of the Ruth Glacier to the summit. Matches existing DB trailhead almost exactly (48.91021,-121.591885 vs sourced 48.9101,-121.5927 — same point).

wa_concerto_in_c_for_drill_and_hammer.name: Grassy saddle (South Face routes)
wa_concerto_in_c_for_drill_and_hammer.note: ~3 hr approach through forest, a tributary crossing, and two gullies to the saddle below Squire Creek Wall's South Face; 14-pitch 5.8 friction slab leads to the summit crest above Buckeye Basin.

wa_concerto_in_c_for_drill_and_hammer.name: Squire Creek Trailhead (Trail #654, end of FS Rd 2040)
wa_concerto_in_c_for_drill_and_hammer.note: Existing DB value confirmed correct against WTA. Road is badly washed out near the end (2002 Jumbo Mountain slide); many parties now park ~1/3 mile short at an informal pullout.

wa_doorway_flake.name: Grassy saddle (South Face routes)
wa_doorway_flake.note: Shares the same ~3 hr approach as the wall's other South Face routes.

wa_doorway_flake.name: Squire Creek Trailhead (Trail #654, end of FS Rd 2040)
wa_doorway_flake.note: Existing DB value confirmed correct against WTA.

wa_skeena26.name: Grassy saddle (South Face routes)
wa_skeena26.note: Brilliant white slab starting near the saddle, mostly 5.4-5.6 with a 5.9 opening pitch.

wa_skeena26.name: Squire Creek Trailhead (Trail #654, end of FS Rd 2040)
wa_skeena26.note: Existing DB value confirmed correct against WTA; multiple CascadeClimbers.com trip reports (FA 9/17/2012, and later linkups) describe this same approach.

wa_spectre_peak_south_route.name: Hannegan Pass
wa_spectre_peak_south_route.note: High point of the maintained Hannegan Pass Trail (#674); leave the trail here to traverse cross-country toward Easy Ridge rather than continuing to Copper Ridge.

wa_spectre_peak_south_route.name: Chilliwack River ford
wa_spectre_peak_south_route.note: Ford the Chilliwack River below Easy Ridge on the climbers' path past Copper Creek before switchbacking back up; can be a cold, thigh-deep crossing in early season.

wa_spectre_peak_south_route.name: Bivy beyond Easy Peak
wa_spectre_peak_south_route.note: Established climbers' bivy near the summit of Easy Peak (6,613'), reached via the Easy Ridge climbers' path gained above Hannegan Pass; typical end of day one.

wa_spectre_peak_south_route.name: Imperfect Impasse
wa_spectre_peak_south_route.note: A notch on Easy Ridge that must be downclimbed and re-ascended to continue toward the Pickets proper; exposed and slower than it looks from a distance.

wa_spectre_peak_south_route.name: Challenger Col
wa_spectre_peak_south_route.note: Snow/glacier col that gains the western slope of the range; parties have noted a bergschrund forming near its top by mid-to-late season.

wa_spectre_peak_south_route.name: Pickle Pass
wa_spectre_peak_south_route.note: Gap below Spectre's serrated south ridge of hoodoos, visible from Frenzel Camp, where the technical climbing on the route begins.

wa_spectre_peak_south_route.name: Hannegan Pass Trailhead
wa_spectre_peak_south_route.note: Matches existing DB entry almost exactly (existing 48.9101,-121.5927 vs. FS/WTA-sourced 48.9102,-121.5941, ~100m diff, within trailhead/parking-area noise). Confirmed as the start point for the 2-day approach (Hannegan Pass -> Easy Ridge -> Pickell Pass) described in the AAC/theclimbingguides trip reports for this route's first ascent.

wa_western_dihedral.name: Grassy saddle (South Face routes)
wa_western_dihedral.note: Climbs the obvious reddish right-facing corner visible from the saddle; crux liebacking/stemming and a finger traverse on pitches 2-3.

wa_western_dihedral.name: Squire Creek Trailhead (Trail #654, end of FS Rd 2040)
wa_western_dihedral.note: Existing DB value confirmed correct against WTA. MP notes ~4 hours trailhead-to-base, then Class 4 scrambling via Skeena26's base to reach this route.

wa_direct_finish.name: Obstruction Point Road pullout at base of Steeple Rock (~2 mi from Hurricane Ridge Visitor Center junction)
wa_direct_finish.note: Not the Hurricane Ridge Visitor Center — that is 2 road-miles away and only the registration point/road start. The spire sits directly beside Obstruction Point Road; climbers park at a pullout at its base.

wa_east_ridge.name: Obstruction Point Road pullout at base of Steeple Rock (~2 mi from Hurricane Ridge Visitor Center junction)
wa_east_ridge.note: Not the Hurricane Ridge Visitor Center — that is 2 road-miles away and only the registration point/road start.

wa_north_ridge.name: Obstruction Point Road pullout at base of Steeple Rock (~2 mi from Hurricane Ridge Visitor Center junction)
wa_north_ridge.note: Not the Hurricane Ridge Visitor Center — that is 2 road-miles away and only the registration point/road start.

wa_wings.name: Obstruction Point Road pullout at base of Steeple Rock (~2 mi from Hurricane Ridge Visitor Center junction)
wa_wings.note: Not the Hurricane Ridge Visitor Center — that is 2 road-miles away and only the registration point/road start.

wa_the_temple_south_ridge.name: Snow Lakes Trailhead
wa_the_temple_south_ridge.note: Corrected from DB's existing value (47.5556, -120.705), which is ~1.3km off the actual parking lot location on Icicle Creek Road, 4.2-4.3 mi from US-2/Icicle Creek Road junction.

wa_tricouni_peak_southwest_slopes.name: Thunder Creek log crossing
wa_tricouni_peak_southwest_slopes.note: The original footbridge over Thunder Creek near mile 6.6 washed out in fall 2017; parties cross via a log felled about 1,000 ft downstream of the old bridge site. Coordinates approximate.

wa_tricouni_peak_southwest_slopes.name: McAllister Camp
wa_tricouni_peak_southwest_slopes.note: Backcountry stock camp where McAllister Creek meets Thunder Creek; leave the maintained trail here and pick up the unmaintained climbers' boot path at the first fork. Coordinates approximate.

wa_tricouni_peak_southwest_slopes.name: Ridge viewpoint
wa_tricouni_peak_southwest_slopes.note: Boot path up the north ridge passes a viewpoint here with the first views of Primus, Tricouni, and neighboring peaks. Coordinates approximate.

wa_tricouni_peak_southwest_slopes.name: Borealis Lake camp
wa_tricouni_peak_southwest_slopes.note: Standard base camp on a flat bench below the Borealis Glacier. Elevation and coordinates are approximate — not precisely confirmed in available trip reports.

wa_tricouni_peak_southwest_slopes.name: Lucky Pass (Primus-Tricouni col)
wa_tricouni_peak_southwest_slopes.note: Reached via roped travel across the Borealis Glacier's west edge, which has retreated and split into upper/lower tiers separated by slabs and cliffs. Elevation and coordinates are approximate.

wa_tricouni_peak_southwest_slopes.name: Thunder Creek Trailhead (Colonial Creek Campground, South Loop)
wa_tricouni_peak_southwest_slopes.note: Existing DB coords (48.6892,-121.0977) are within ~0.4mi of this NPS/WTA-sourced point and are a reasonable match for the same trailhead; both refer to the Thunder Creek Trail start at Colonial Creek Campground on Hwy 20. This is a legitimately long/remote approach (24-mile round trip: Thunder Creek Trail to McAllister camp, off-trail to Borealis Lake, across Borealis Glacier to Lucky Pass) — the ~12km straight-line distance from summit is expected, not a data error.

wa_south_face.name: The Ledge Bivy
wa_south_face.note: Common bivy area partway up to Burgundy Col.

wa_south_face.name: Burgundy Col
wa_south_face.note: Separates the Wine Spires from Vasiliki Ridge; Vasiliki Tower stands on the left entering the col.

wa_south_face.name: Early Winters Creek Trailhead
wa_south_face.note: Roadside pull-off on SR-20 near milepost 165-166, ~4 mi east of Washington Pass; cross Early Winters Creek then climb ~3 mi to Burgundy Col.

wa_whatcom_peak_southwest_route.name: Hannegan Pass
wa_whatcom_peak_southwest_route.note: High point of the maintained Hannegan Pass Trail; the route leaves good tread here and drops steeply into the Chilliwack River valley toward the Brush Creek approach.

wa_whatcom_peak_southwest_route.name: Chilliwack River ford
wa_whatcom_peak_southwest_route.note: Unbridged ford of the Chilliwack River reported thigh-deep at typical mid-summer flow; can run much higher and more dangerous during snowmelt or after rain.

wa_whatcom_peak_southwest_route.name: Graybeal Camp
wa_whatcom_peak_southwest_route.note: Established camp about 2 miles up the Brush Creek Trail; the camp itself is dry by late summer, so fill water bottles at Brush Creek roughly a half mile before arriving.

wa_whatcom_peak_southwest_route.name: Whatcom Pass
wa_whatcom_peak_southwest_route.note: Trail high point and standard base-camp area for the climb; junction with the Tapto Lakes path and the climbers' route onto the Whatcom Glacier.

wa_whatcom_peak_southwest_route.name: Whatcom Glacier traverse
wa_whatcom_peak_southwest_route.note: Traverse the east side of the retreating Whatcom Glacier around 5,200-5,500 ft; NPS and guidebook reports warn of icefall and crevasse hazard here, worsening after mid-summer as the ice has thinned.

wa_whatcom_peak_southwest_route.name: Hannegan Pass Trailhead
wa_whatcom_peak_southwest_route.note: Same trailhead. NPS trip account describes traversing Whatcom Peak's east side / 'Whatcom Glacier route' from Whatcom Pass (reached via Hannegan Pass Trailhead).

wa_gato_negro.name: Whine Spire (Gato Negro topout)
wa_gato_negro.note: 12-pitch alpine trad route (5.10a/b) on the sub-peak east of Silver Star Mountain; topout elevation is approximate.

wa_gato_negro.name: SR-20 Wine Spires / Silver Star pullout (~MP 165, ~4 mi east of Washington Pass)
wa_gato_negro.note: Corrects existing DB value (Blue Lake Trailhead), which is on the wrong side of Washington Pass entirely. Climbers park at this pullout, descend to and cross Early Winters Creek, then climb a steep climbers trail to the Bench (~6,500-6,700ft) below Burgundy Col, from which all Wine Spires routes (including Whine Spire/Gato Negro) and Silver Star's standard route are reached.
